title: Jonah and the Horizon
premise: Juniper Brightwater smuggles stolen memories between the silent colonies of the Meridian System, hiding in the gaps of a civilization that cut itself in two after the Sundering. When gravity stutters for nine seconds system-wide, she learns it was a countdown signal from Earth's dying relay—and that her own fragmented childhood memories contain the decryption key both halves of humanity have been hunting. Hunted by the orbital authority and the colony underground alike, Juniper must choose which half of humanity wakes first from cryosleep, knowing the other half may never forgive her. She splits the key, waking neither side alone but forcing them to open the sleep-vaults together, as Earth's last transmission finally loops to silence.
about_author: E. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent six years listening to dead frequencies before turning to fiction. They write near-future science fiction about people who carry impossible things across impossible distances.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: Juniper runs a memory shipment through Meridian customs hidden inside a lullaby recording, narrating her own careful invisibility. A routine scan almost catches her when the inspector lingers on one memory that isn't hers—a snowfall she has no explanation for. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a life built on carrying other people's pasts while having none of her own.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: In dock at Ceres Hollow, gravity fails across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; ships drift, people float, then everything slams back. Juniper's POV captures the eerie silence afterward—every screen in the port displaying the same nine-second timestamp. Emotional beat: dread blooming into wonder, the sense that the universe just said her name.

chapters.title: The Buyer Who Knew Her Name
chapters.summary: A client named Ovid Rell offers Juniper an obscene sum for 'whatever you were holding during the flicker.' She refuses, but he leaves her a datachip: a partial image of herself as a child, standing before the Earth relay antenna. Emotional beat: vertigo—the smuggler discovers she is cargo she never knew she carried.

chapters.title: What the Snowfall Remembers
chapters.summary: Juniper decrypts her own anomalous memories with help from Tamsin, her fence and only friend. The snowfall resolves into the day of the Sundering: she was at the relay station, and someone implanted the key in her mind before wiping her. Emotional beat: grief for a self that was taken from her, and fury at whoever took it.

chapters.title: Two Halves, One Key
chapters.summary: Juniper learns the truth: the cryosleep vaults of the Inner Belt and the Outer Reach each hold half of humanity, and the flicker was Earth's relay announcing its final countdown. The decryption key is split—one half in her head, one half somewhere on Earth's dead loop. POV shifts briefly to Ovid, revealing he serves the Inner Belt authority. Emotional beat: the crushing weight of being the hinge of history.

chapters.title: Running the Long Route
chapters.summary: Juniper flees outward along her old smuggling routes, pursued by Inner Belt enforcers and courted by Outer Reach separatists who want her half of the key. Tamsin sacrifices their ship and cover identity to buy her escape. Emotional beat: the cost of belonging—Juniper realizes every bond she made while invisible is now a target on someone else's back.

chapters.title: The Relay at the End of the World
chapters.summary: Reaching the derelict Earth relay, Juniper finds Ovid waiting, and the loop's second key fragment encoded in the transmission itself. He offers a deal: wake the Inner Belt alone, let the Outer Reach sleep forever. As they argue, the countdown accelerates—the loop will end in days, erasing the fragment permanently. Emotional beat: temptation of the easy, unforgivable choice.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds, Reversed
chapters.summary: Climax. Juniper realizes the flicker wasn't a signal—it was a handshake protocol, and the system itself can be made to repeat it, broadcasting the completed key to both vaults simultaneously. She merges her memories with the loop as enforcers breach the relay, nearly losing herself inside her own restored past. Emotional beat: surrendering the self she fought to recover so that everyone else might keep theirs.

chapters.title: Waking Is a Choice We Make Together
chapters.summary: Both vaults receive the key; neither side wakes without the other's confirmation code, forcing cooperation for the first time since the Sundering. Juniper, memory-frayed and half-dissolved, is found by Tamsin and Outer Reach medics who argue over who gets to claim her. Emotional beat: exhaustion and fragile hope—survival achieved, but at a price still being counted.

chapters.title: The Horizon Keeps Its Promises
chapters.summary: Months later, Juniper pilots a diplomatic run between worlds that are learning to speak again, no longer invisible but not yet known—even to herself. Some memories never returned; she decides some weren't hers to keep. Watching the first joint wake-cycle begin, she chooses to stay on the long route. Emotional beat: quiet peace—belonging not to a place or a past, but to the crossing between.
